Champurrado Espumoso

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Champurrado Espumoso is a traditional Mexican thick and frothy chocolate drink made with masa harina, served especially during Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation) on February 2nd. This warm, comforting beverage is enjoyed as part of the festivities, often accompanying tamales, symbolizing warmth and community during the winter season.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (960 ml) whole milk
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) piloncillo or dark brown sugar, chopped
  • 2 oz (56 g) Mexican chocolate, chopped (such as Abuelita or Ibarra)
  • 1 cinnamon stick
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/4 tsp salt

Method

  1. In a medium saucepan, heat the milk over medium heat until warm but not boiling.
  2. In a separate bowl, dissolve the masa harina in 1 cup (240 ml) of warm water, whisking until smooth and no lumps remain.
  3. Add the dissolved masa harina mixture to the warm milk, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
  4. Add the piloncillo, cinnamon stick, and salt to the saucepan, continuing to stir until the piloncillo dissolves completely.
  5. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate and continue stirring until the chocolate melts and the mixture thickens, about 10 minutes.
  6. Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the vanilla extract.
  7. Using a hand whisk or a traditional molinillo (wooden whisk), vigorously whisk the champurrado to create a frothy, foamy top.
  8. Serve hot in mugs, enjoying the rich, thick, and frothy texture.

Tips

  • Use a molinillo to achieve the traditional frothy texture for an authentic experience.
  • Adjust the sweetness by adding more or less piloncillo according to taste.
  • For a dairy-free version, substitute whole milk with almond or oat milk, but the texture may be slightly different.
